How to Apply
If you’re interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in Earth and Environmental Science, follow these steps to get started:
Step 1: Get to Know Our Faculty and Department Research
PhD students work under the mentorship and guidance of a Department faculty member. View the list of Earth and Environmental Science faculty and visit their lab websites, read through their publications, and study their research. It is important to find a faculty member that you connect with, and that can help guide your future dissertation work. They will not be the only faculty supporting you, but your advisor will play a key role in your training and research.
If you don’t find a faculty member that matches your research goals, you might be a better fit at a different Penn Department or another university. It is important to find the right program for you!
Step 2: Reach Out to The Faculty Member
Once you find a faculty member you would like to study with, send them an email briefly describing your own research goals, why you want to work with them, and asking if they are currently taking PhD students. If there is a potential good fit, the faculty member will reply to you to set up a virtual meeting. Having these conversations early helps you find a mentor and program that fits your goals. You are much more likely to have a successful PhD application if you can make these connections with specific faculty members.
Step 3: Apply!
The School of Arts and Sciences accepts PhD applications annually. The next application deadline is Tuesday, December 8, 2026 at 11:59PM EST. Accepted PhD candidates would start their study in Fall 2027.
Apply here: apply.graduateadmissions.upenn.edu/apply/
Penn Graduate Division of Arts and Sciences PhD Application Information
Request for program information
Earth and Environmental Science Admissions Requirements
The GRE General Test is not required. Geoscience is a broad field, and we welcome applicants with undergraduate degrees in physics, chemistry, biology, computer science, engineering, mathematics, as well as in geology.
Personal Statement
In the personal statement, all Ph.D. applications within the Graduate Division of Arts & Sciences should address the following:
Please describe how your background and academic experiences have influenced your decision to pursue a graduate degree and led you to apply to Penn. Your essay should detail your specific research interests and intellectual goals within your chosen field. Please provide information about your educational trajectory, intellectual curiosity and academic ambitions. If you have experienced limited access to resources or opportunities in your field of study, please feel free to share how these and how they have affected the course of your education.
Fee Waivers
A limited number of application fee waivers are available for applicants who demonstrate clear and compelling financial hardship. The Graduate Division of Arts and Sciences oversees the waiver process, which is completed through the application.
For more information, please refer to their Application Information page (waiver information is near the bottom). Applicants should submit requests at least 2 weeks prior to the application deadline.
All waiver requests must be made through the application. Please do not send your request or any personal information by email.
